meta.summary: SiliconForge lets a model propose RTL and lets formal proof, equivalence checking and layout decide, and it publishes its null results.

picks.what: An open RTL toolkit where a language model may propose a design but formal proof, equivalence checking and layout on open-source EDA decide whether it is accepted.
picks.area: AI for chip design (RTL, verification, lint, EDA flow automation, RISC-V)
picks.fitWhy: Chip design is my home ground, and every gate in its pipeline is a tool verdict rather than a model's opinion.
picks.caution: A one-person project a week old with five stars. AGPL, with a separate commercial licence offered. Its own results are small samples and it says so.

picks.what: A research multi-agent system that generates RTL and checks it with simulation, temporal tracing and formal verification.
picks.area: AI for chip design (RTL, verification, lint, EDA flow automation, RISC-V)
picks.fitWhy: Combines simulation and formal checks around generated RTL, close to how I would want an agent bounded in hardware work.
picks.caution: Research code from a paper. GitHub reports no recognised licence (NOASSERTION).

picks.what: A research multi-agent system that writes Python-based testbenches to verify RTL automatically.
picks.area: AI for chip design (RTL, verification, lint, EDA flow automation, RISC-V)
picks.fitWhy: Agent-written testbenches are worth reading for how they judge their own checks.
picks.caution: No licence file, so reuse is not permitted by default. Last pushed in December 2025.

picks.what: One interface for language models to call formal tools such as SMT and SAT solvers, model checkers and provers, each in its own container.
picks.fitWhy: A uniform, containerised way to hand formal tools to an agent fits my preference for deterministic checks.

picks.what: A RISC-V CPU that its author says was designed and verified by a local AI agent, with the prompt and progress log published.
picks.area: AI for chip design (RTL, verification, lint, EDA flow automation, RISC-V)
picks.fitWhy: The published prompt and progress log could show how far an agent gets on real RTL, but the claims are the author's.
picks.caution: Claims not verified. GitHub reports no recognised licence.

picks.what: An MCP server that connects AI agents to remote Linux EDA clusters for design and verification.
picks.area: AI for chip design (RTL, verification, lint, EDA flow automation, RISC-V)
picks.fitWhy: Agent access to EDA tools is a real need, but this gives an agent a path into compute clusters.
picks.caution: It sits between an agent and remote machines. Review exactly what it can run before connecting it to anything real.

picks.what: Agent skills for RTL design, SystemVerilog and UVM verification, written Chinese-first.
picks.area: AI for chip design (RTL, verification, lint, EDA flow automation, RISC-V)
picks.fitWhy: Skills for my own domain are worth comparing with how I would write them.
